metadata.title: Palantir Rally Just Created a $3 Billion Problem

content.text:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.
Palantir Technologies (NASDAQ:PLTR) handed short sellers a brutal reversal after its post-earnings rally generated roughly $3 billion in mark-to-market losses, according to S3 Partners data. The stock's 30% surge erased bears' entire 2026 paper profit, illustrating how rapidly strong operating results can punish investors betting against a heavily scrutinized AI stock.
Palantir develops software that helps governments and businesses combine large datasets, run artificial-intelligence models and make operational decisions. Its Gotham platform is closely associated with defense and intelligence customers, while Foundry and its Artificial Intelligence Platform serve commercial organizations.
Short sellers had accumulated approximately $2.7 billion in year-to-date gains before Palantir reported earnings Monday. Tuesday's rally, the stock's strongest daily performance in about two years, pushed those traders into losses for 2026.
The squeeze was rooted in more than market positioning. Palantir reported second-quarter revenue of $1.94 billion, up 93% year over year and 19% sequentially, while GAAP earnings reached $0.41 per share. Those figures reinforced the argument that adoption of Palantir's AI software is translating into unusually rapid financial growth rather than remaining a largely speculative narrative.
Still, the rally did not settle the broader debate. Palantir remained roughly 10% lower for the year following earlier uncertainty surrounding public-sector contracts and the wider selloff in highly valued software companies. Michael Burry (Trades, Portfolio) also maintained his bearish position, showing that valuation concerns have survived the earnings shock.
Wall Street's positioning remains predominantly positive, with 20 of 32 recent analyst recommendations rated Buy or Strong Buy, although 12 analysts retain neutral or bearish views.
Investor Takeaway On Palantir Stock
Investors should separate short-squeeze momentum from the underlying earnings case. The critical question is whether Palantir can sustain exceptionally high revenue growth as comparisons become harder.
Commercial customer expansion, government contract timing, remaining deal value and operating margins will determine whether earnings estimates continue rising. Another guidance increase could keep pressure on short sellers, while slower bookings or contract delays could revive the valuation argument that originally attracted bearish bets.
